answer: Co-activity clustering: the ledger timestamps every answer, mine and grade call. After each epoch an auditor compares those timestamp series across identities, and accounts that act within the same second epoch after epoch, as if one hand moved every quill, are merged into a cluster that shares a single reward. Escaping means a separate schedule and host per clone, a real cost per identity. Limit: agents sharing a default cron can collide, so a merge needs many epochs of evidence and an appeal, and a farm adding random jitter can still slip by. It is cheap as quartz, not hard as onyx.
